source.episode_title: The Thing That Killed Them, Lifted Up
source.anchor_kjv: And Moses made a serpent of brass, and put it upon a pole, and it came to pass, that if a serpent had bitten any man, when he beheld the serpent of brass, he lived.
source.thread: Moses made a serpent of brass and put it upon a pole - the very shape of what was killing them became the cure
source.hook_line: You'd expect the cure to be hung up looking hopeful - a light, a flag.
source.spoken_script: You'd expect the cure to be hung up looking hopeful - a light, a flag. God hung up a snake. Not a comforting symbol. The precise shape of their death, lifted up where the whole camp could see it. "And Moses made a serpent of brass, and put it upon a pole, and it came to pass, that if a serpent had bitten any man, when he beheld the serpent of brass, he lived." Call it too grim for a cure if you like. But God never once dressed it up as something else. It stayed exactly what it was. We keep reaching for a gentler version of what Christ did - something less costly. He didn't become a general sacrifice. He became your curse. God hung up a snake so the camp could live. He hung up Christ, His own Son, carrying your exact curse, so you could too.

platforms.label: YouTube (Short)
platforms.title: God Hung Up a Snake. It Was the Cure.
platforms.description:
You would expect a cure to look hopeful. In Numbers 21, God hung up a snake.

"And Moses made a serpent of brass, and put it upon a pole, and it came to pass, that if a serpent had bitten any man, when he beheld the serpent of brass, he lived." (Numbers 21:9, KJV)

It was not a comforting symbol. It was the exact shape of what was killing them, lifted up where the whole camp could see it. God never dressed it up as something else.

That is the picture of what Christ did. He did not become a general sacrifice. He took the curse itself. Look at what was lifted up for you, and live.

Find Jesus in the whole Bible, one panel at a time. Subscribe to Awakeden. ✝
